text: Apple annual revenue by fiscal year (fiscal year ends late September; dollars in billions): FY2016 $215.64, FY2019 $260.17, FY2020 $274.52 (+5.5%), FY2021 $365.82 (+33.3%), FY2022 $394.33 (+7.8%), FY2023 $383.29 (-2.8%), FY2024 $391.04 (+2.0%).

Company Background
The Company designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells a variety of related services. The Company's fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September.

Segments
The Company manages its business primarily on a geographic basis. The Company's reportable segments consist of the Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific. Americas includes both North and South America. Europe includes European countries, as well as India, the Middle East and Africa. Greater China includes China mainland, Hong Kong and Taiwan. Rest of Asia Pacific includes Australia and those Asian countries not included in the Company's other reportable segments.

Human Capital
As of September 28, 2024, the Company had approximately 164,000 full-time equivalent employees.

Macroeconomic and Industry Risks
The Company's operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions and adverse economic conditions can materially adversely affect the Company's business, results of operations and financial condition. The Company has international operations with sales outside the U.S. representing a majority of the Company's total net sales.

Global markets for the Company's products and services are highly competitive and subject to rapid technological change, and the Company may be unable to compete effectively in these markets. The Company has a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer and tablet markets.

The Company's products and services may be affected from time to time by design and manufacturing defects. The introduction of new and complex technologies, such as artificial intelligence features, can increase these and other safety risks, including exposing users to harmful, inaccurate or other negative content and experiences.

Legal and Regulatory Compliance Risks
The Company's global operations are subject to complex and changing laws and regulations worldwide, which exposes the Company to potential liabilities, increased costs and other adverse effects on the Company's business, including antitrust; privacy, data security and data localization; digital platforms; machine learning and artificial intelligence.

Digital Markets Act Investigations
On March 25, 2024, the European Commission announced that it had opened two formal noncompliance investigations against the Company under the DMA. If the Commission makes a final determination that there has been a violation, it can issue a cease and desist order and may impose fines up to 10% of the Company's annual worldwide net sales.

Department of Justice Lawsuit
On March 21, 2024, the U.S. Department of Justice and a number of state and district attorneys general filed a civil antitrust lawsuit against the Company alleging monopolization or attempted monopolization in the markets for "performance smartphones" and "smartphones" in violation of U.S. antitrust laws.

Product, Service and Software Announcements (Fiscal Year 2024)
Third Quarter 2024 included Apple Intelligence, a personal intelligence system that uses generative models.
Fourth Quarter 2024 included iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro and iPhone 16 Pro Max; Apple Watch Series 10; and AirPods 4.

Segment Operating Performance
Net sales by reportable segment for 2024, 2023 and 2022 (dollars in millions):

Americas: $167,045 (2024), +3% change, $162,560 (2023), -4% change, $169,658 (2022)
Europe: $101,328 (2024), +7% change, $94,294 (2023), -1% change, $95,118 (2022)
Greater China: $66,952 (2024), -8% change, $72,559 (2023), -2% change, $74,200 (2022)
Japan: $25,052 (2024), +3% change, $24,257 (2023), -7% change, $25,977 (2022)
Rest of Asia Pacific: $30,658 (2024), +4% change, $29,615 (2023), +1% change, $29,375 (2022)
Total net sales: $391,035 (2024), +2% change, $383,285 (2023), -3% change, $394,328 (2022)

Greater China net sales decreased during 2024 compared to 2023 due primarily to lower net sales of iPhone and iPad. The weakness in the renminbi relative to the U.S. dollar had an unfavorable year-over-year impact on Greater China net sales during 2024.

Products and Services Performance
Net sales by category for 2024, 2023 and 2022 (dollars in millions):

iPhone: $201,183 (2024), 0% change, $200,583 (2023), -2% change, $205,489 (2022)
Mac: $29,984 (2024), +2% change, $29,357 (2023), -27% change, $40,177 (2022)
iPad: $26,694 (2024), -6% change, $28,300 (2023), -3% change, $29,292 (2022)
Wearables, Home and Accessories: $37,005 (2024), -7% change, $39,845 (2023), -3% change, $41,241 (2022)
Services: $96,169 (2024), +13% change, $85,200 (2023), +9% change, $78,129 (2022)
Total net sales: $391,035 (2024), +2% change, $383,285 (2023), -3% change, $394,328 (2022)

Services net sales increased during 2024 compared to 2023 due primarily to higher net sales from advertising, the App Store and cloud services.

Gross Margin
Products and Services gross margin and gross margin percentage for 2024, 2023 and 2022 (dollars in millions):

Products gross margin: $109,633 (2024), $108,803 (2023), $114,728 (2022)
Services gross margin: $71,050 (2024), $60,345 (2023), $56,054 (2022)
Total gross margin: $180,683 (2024), $169,148 (2023), $170,782 (2022)
Products gross margin percentage: 37.2% (2024), 36.5% (2023), 36.3% (2022)
Services gross margin percentage: 73.9% (2024), 70.8% (2023), 71.7% (2022)
Total gross margin percentage: 46.2% (2024), 44.1% (2023), 43.3% (2022)

Products gross margin and Products gross margin percentage increased during 2024 compared to 2023 due to cost savings, partially offset by a different Products mix and the weakness in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar.

Operating Expenses
Operating expenses for 2024, 2023 and 2022 (dollars in millions):

Research and development: $31,370 (2024), +5% change, $29,915 (2023), +14% change, $26,251 (2022)
R&D percentage of total net sales: 8% (2024), 8% (2023), 7% (2022)
Selling, general and administrative: $26,097 (2024), +5% change, $24,932 (2023), -1% change, $25,094 (2022)
Total operating expenses: $57,467 (2024), +5% change, $54,847 (2023), +7% change, $51,345 (2022)

The growth in R&D expense during 2024 compared to 2023 was driven primarily by increases in headcount-related expenses.

Provision for Income Taxes
Provision for income taxes, effective tax rate for 2024, 2023 and 2022:

Provision for income taxes: $29,749 million (2024), $16,741 million (2023), $19,300 million (2022)
Effective tax rate: 24.1% (2024), 14.7% (2023), 16.2% (2022)
Statutory federal income tax rate: 21% (all years)

The Company's effective tax rate for 2024 was higher than the statutory federal income tax rate due primarily to a one-time income tax charge of $10.2 billion, net, related to the State Aid Decision and state income taxes, partially offset by a lower effective tax rate on foreign earnings.

Liquidity and Capital Resources
The Company's balances of unrestricted cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $140.8 billion as of September 28, 2024.
As of September 28, 2024, the Company had outstanding fixed-rate notes with varying maturities for an aggregate principal amount of $97.3 billion.
During 2024, the Company repurchased $95.0 billion of its common stock and paid dividends and dividend equivalents of $15.2 billion.

Amazon annual revenue by calendar year (dollars in billions): 2016 $135.99, 2017 $177.87 (+30.8%), 2018 $232.89 (+30.9%), 2019 $280.52 (+20.5%), 2020 $386.06 (+37.6%), 2021 $469.82 (+21.7%), 2022 $513.98 (+9.4%), 2023 $574.78 (+11.8%), 2024 $637.96 (+11.0%).

Amazon has posted nine consecutive years of revenue growth through 2024. Amazon's business is organized into three primary segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). AWS is Amazon's highest-margin segment and has been a primary driver of overall operating profit even in years when the retail segments operated on thin margins.

filed_date: Compiled from public filings, current as of 2025
text: Amazon's revenue mix spans e-commerce retail (North America and International segments) and cloud infrastructure (AWS). Unlike a pure retailer, a meaningful and growing share of Amazon's profitability comes from AWS rather than the retail operations, even though retail represents the larger share of total revenue.

Alphabet's revenue is driven predominantly by Google advertising (Search, YouTube, Network), with Google Cloud and other bets contributing a smaller but growing share. 2021 saw the sharpest growth as digital ad spend rebounded strongly post-pandemic.

section: ANNUAL NET REVENUE HISTORY -- ACCOUNTING NOTE
text: Goldman Sachs annual net revenue (dollars in billions, approximate): 2021 (peak) $59.34, declining in subsequent years amid a slower investment banking and trading environment, then recovering to approximately $58.28 by 2025. Like JPMorgan Chase, this is net revenue, not gross sales -- Goldman Sachs is an investment bank, and its revenue is driven by trading, investment banking fees, and asset/wealth management, not product sales. Direct comparison to a non-bank's revenue is not meaningful without accounting for this difference.

filed_date: Compiled from public filings, current as of 2025
section: ANNUAL NET REVENUE HISTORY -- ACCOUNTING NOTE
text: JPMorgan Chase reported net revenue of $158.1 billion in 2023, a then-record high for the company. IMPORTANT ACCOUNTING NOTE: bank "revenue" is fundamentally not comparable to a technology or consumer company's revenue. Banks report net revenue (interest income minus interest expense, plus fee-based income), not gross sales, because their core business is lending money and managing risk, not selling a product at a fixed price. Comparing a bank's net revenue directly against a tech company's gross revenue significantly understates the bank's actual scale of financial activity.

text:
Meta Platforms annual revenue by calendar year (dollars in billions): 2023 $134.90, 2024 $164.50 (+21.9%). Growth in 2024 was driven by digital advertising demand and improved ad targeting and pricing, following a slower growth period in 2022 amid a broader digital ad market slowdown and rising competition for user attention.

Meta's revenue is overwhelmingly derived from advertising across Facebook, Instagram, and its other apps. Reality Labs (VR/AR/metaverse investments) represents a small fraction of revenue but a large share of operating losses, reflecting Meta's long-term bet on the category.

Microsoft annual revenue by fiscal year (fiscal year ends June 30; dollars in billions): FY2016 $91.15, FY2017 $96.57, FY2018 $110.36, FY2019 $125.84, FY2020 $143.01 (+13.7%), FY2021 $168.09 (+17.5%), FY2022 $198.27 (+18.0%), FY2023 $211.91 (+6.9%), FY2024 $245.12 (+15.7%). Nine consecutive years of revenue growth.

General
Microsoft is a technology company committed to making digital technology and artificial intelligence ("AI") available broadly and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more.

We have entered a new age of AI that will fundamentally transform productivity for every individual, organization, and industry on earth. Microsoft's AI offerings, including Copilot and our Copilot stack, are already orchestrating a new era of AI transformation.

We have a long-term partnership with OpenAI, a leading AI research and deployment company. We deploy OpenAI's models across our consumer and enterprise products. As OpenAI's exclusive cloud provider, Azure powers all of OpenAI's workloads.

Operating Segments
We operate our business and report our financial performance using three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing.

Productivity and Business Processes segment primarily comprises Office Commercial, Office Consumer, LinkedIn, and Dynamics business solutions.

Intelligent Cloud segment primarily comprises Server products and cloud services, including Azure and other cloud services; SQL Server, Windows Server; and Nuance and GitHub.

More Personal Computing segment primarily comprises Windows, Devices (including Surface), Gaming (including Xbox, Activision Blizzard content), and Search and news advertising (Bing, Copilot, Microsoft Edge).

Human Capital
As of June 30, 2024, we employed approximately 228,000 people on a full-time basis, 126,000 in the U.S. and 102,000 internationally.

We are investing in artificial intelligence ("AI") across the entire company and infusing generative AI capabilities into our consumer and commercial offerings. We expect AI technology and services to be a highly competitive and rapidly evolving market, and new competitors continue to enter the market. We will bear significant development and operational costs to build and support the AI models, services, platforms, and infrastructure necessary to meet the needs of our customers.

Issues in the development and use of AI may result in reputational or competitive harm or liability. We are building AI into many of our offerings, including our productivity services. AI algorithms or training methodologies may be flawed. Datasets may be overbroad, insufficient, or contain biased information. Content generated by AI systems may be offensive, illegal, inaccurate, or otherwise harmful. These risks may arise from current copyright infringement and other claims related to AI training and output, new and proposed legislation and regulations, such as the European Union's AI Act and the U.S.'s AI Executive Order.

Cybersecurity: As previously disclosed in our Form 8-K filed with the SEC on January 19, 2024 and amended on March 8, 2024, beginning in late November 2023, a nation-state associated threat actor used a password spray attack to compromise a legacy test account and, in turn, gain access to Microsoft email accounts.

Acquisitions: In March 2022 we completed our acquisition of Nuance Communications, Inc., and in October 2023 we completed our acquisition of Activision Blizzard, Inc. In January 2023 we announced the third phase of our OpenAI strategic partnership. The Federal Trade Commission continues to challenge our Activision Blizzard acquisition and could, if successful, alter or unwind the transaction.

Competition: Our AI offerings compete with AI products from hyperscalers such as Amazon and Google, as well as products from other emerging competitors, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, and other open source offerings, many of which are also current or potential partners.

section: FROM THE FY2024 PROXY STATEMENT / SHAREHOLDER LETTER
text:
Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $137.4 billion.
Office Commercial products and cloud services revenue increased 14%.
Xbox content and services revenue increased 50%, driven by 44 points of net impact from the Activision Blizzard acquisition.
Microsoft delivered strong results for its shareholders, including a return of over $34 billion in the form of share repurchases and dividends in fiscal year 2024.

filed_date: Compiled from public filings, current as of 2025
text:
Netflix annual revenue by calendar year (dollars in billions): 2020 $25.0, 2021 $29.7 (+18.8%), 2022 $31.6 (+6.5%, growth slowed sharply amid subscriber saturation in mature markets), 2023 $33.72 (+6.7%), 2024 $39.0 (+15.6%, reaccelerated on ad-tier subscriber growth and the password-sharing crackdown converting freeloaders to paid accounts).

Netflix's growth trajectory shows a clear pattern: rapid pandemic-era growth (2020-2021), a sharp slowdown (2022) as the streaming market matured and competition intensified, followed by a deliberate strategic reacceleration (2023-2024) driven by two specific initiatives -- the ad-supported tier and password-sharing enforcement.

text:
Nvidia annual revenue by fiscal year (fiscal year ends late January; dollars in billions): FY2023 (ended Jan 2023) $26.97, FY2024 (ended Jan 2024) $60.92 (+126%, more than doubling year-over-year). This growth was driven overwhelmingly by AI data center GPU demand, particularly for training and running large language models, representing one of the fastest large-scale revenue ramps of any major public company in recent history.

Nvidia's revenue is concentrated in its Data Center segment (AI/ML infrastructure GPUs), with Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive as smaller segments.

filed_date: Compiled from public filings, current as of 2025
text: PayPal annual net revenue (dollars in billions): FY2021 $25.4 (+18%), FY2024 $31.79. PayPal's revenue growth decelerated substantially after 2021 as e-commerce growth normalized following the pandemic-era surge, and competition in digital payments intensified from both traditional card networks and newer fintech entrants.

filed_date: Compiled from public filings, current as of 2025
text:
Tesla annual revenue by calendar year (dollars in billions): 2023 $96.77, 2024 $97.69 (+0.9%, roughly flat). Growth slowed considerably compared to Tesla's historical pace amid intensified EV competition, multiple rounds of price cuts to defend market share, and softer demand growth in key markets.

Tesla's revenue includes automotive sales/leasing, energy generation and storage, and services. Automotive remains the large majority of total revenue.

filed_date: Compiled from public filings, current as of 2025
text: Visa annual revenue by fiscal year (fiscal year ends September; dollars in billions): FY2023 $32.65, FY2024 $35.93 (+10.0%). Visa's revenue is driven primarily by payments volume, transaction processing fees, and international transaction/cross-border fees -- Visa itself does not issue cards or extend credit; it operates the payments network that banks and merchants use.
